title: Five-town frozen-citation date audit and published-page candidate ledger

result.meaning: 387 is a count of candidate identifier correspondences, including conflicts; it is not a count of verified originals, distinct historical events, or resolved queue items.

frozen_input.scope: Existing event.place first comma-separated component exactly equals one of the five town names, with its expected state; group the existing citation records by strict /1:1: identifier. This reproduces the five original town counts.

date_audit.method: Read only the event date at the end of each existing citation. Do not use the collection title date span, access/retrieval timestamp, or a proposed date from an external compilation.
date_audit.old_implementation_status: The diagnostic expression reproduces all five previously reported date/no-year counts exactly. The old implementation was not recovered, so attributing its behavior to that specific expression is an inference; the omissions themselves are directly demonstrated in the frozen citations.
date_audit.literal_date_warning: Date-bearing does not mean historically correct. Literal 1427 and 1904 claims are preserved as date-bearing conflicts. Dual years are retained without silent calendar conversion.

findings: The Society page title 1729–1843 is not uniform coverage for all underlying series.
Births Vol. 1 is labeled 1725–1844; the index includes one 1724 entry and omits the sole 1844 entry. The 1865 transcription was made from older damaged volumes.
Marriages Vol. 1A is labeled 1729–1900; the Society index covers 1729–1843. Its sequential entry numbers are not original page numbers.
Deaths Vol. 1 covers 1725–1843. The notes report entries in 1725 and 1727 and none in 1726 or 1728.
The 1908 published compilation supplies printed-page candidates beyond the Society index period, including an Isaac Bullard birth in 1726 and a Luther Rockwood marriage in 1846.
The official inventory confirms Town Records Town of Chelmsford, 1650–1750, 410 pages, and Chelmsford Town Record, 1710–1774, 278 pages.
A separate 314-page first/second-book copy is dated March 21, 1892, with original coverage unspecified. Inventory item numbers are not proved manuscript volume numbers.
These are general town-record holdings; broad date coverage does not establish the presence or original page of a vital event.
The 117 main-scope candidates comprise 23 full-date citations and 94 year-only citations. Five additional Chelmsford Center identifiers are retained separately.
The 1911 Baldwin compilation provides candidates for 97 of 99 identifiers; exact original holdings and manuscript citations are still unverified.
A compilation or collection town cannot be treated as the event location. One actual candidate specifies a Milton marriage; another identifies the groom as of Holliston.
Reciprocal spouse entries and multiple participant roles are not independent historical events. The 1724 boundary alone does not prove that the Sherborn and Holliston groups are disjoint events.
The official Connecticut table records establishment in Massachusetts in 1674 and annexation to Connecticut in May 1749.
The Barbour guide explains original town/volume/page source references and identifies both published and bound-index routes for Suffield.
Kent Memorial Library describes early Barbour, Loomis and church records for 1670–1820, with later records at Town Hall; its holdings inventory is dated August 2016.
These collection routes are not exact page matches for the 76 identifiers. Pre-1749 jurisdiction alone does not prove that records reside only in Massachusetts.
The clerk describes vault research with appointments recommended, not mandatory.
The 1741–1844 general online index on the clerk page concerns land records and cannot establish vital-record coverage.
The State Library guide identifies Salisbury vital records, 1740–1905, on microfilm 3966, and Barbour coverage 1741–1846.
Early vital entries are dispersed across town-meeting volumes 1 and 2, land records volume 1, justice-court records, and vital records volume 3.
All 56 date-bearing frozen citations have years 1748–1791, within the described scope; this does not verify any individual entry.
